newsitem.title: USA: FMC to pay $13 mln in settlement - attorney.
newsitem.headline: FMC to pay $13 mln in settlement - attorney.

text.p: FMC Corp has agreed to pay the federal government $13 million to settle a whistleblower case, according to a statement from the whistleblower's law firm.
The whistleblower charged FMC, maker of the Bradley Fighting Vehicle, with inflating costs to be reimbursed by the U.S. Army.
The whistleblower, Robert Neargarder, a mid-level manager in FMC's ground systems division in San Jose, Calif., will receive $2.86 million of the $13 million settlement.
The company did not admit wrongdoing under the settlement.
"We regret that out proceedures did not prevent the issue," said company spokeswoman Pat Brozowski. "We have since improved our proceedures."
Neargarder was represented by Eric Havian of Phillips & Cohen of Washington and San Francisco.
